Abstract.AbstractText: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the most common oncological conditions s worldwide, to date, MicroRNA 1290 (miRNA) has been demonstrated to regulate its progression. We studied the role of miR-1290 in CRC progression. The gene was upregulated in CRC tissues and cells, its overexpression promoted CRC cell proliferation analyzed by MTT assay, colony formation assay and soft agar growth assay. IN addition, miR-1290 knockdown inhibited CRC cell proliferation. We also found that miR-1290 overexpression reduced p27 level and increased Cyclin D1 level both in mRNA and protein levels, while miR-1290 knockdown increased p27 and reduced Cyclin D1 (confirming miR-1290 promoted CRC cell proliferation). Inositol phospholipid phosphatase inositol Polyphosphate 4-Phosphatase B (INPP4B) was the target of miR-1290, luciferase reporter assay revealed miR-1290 directly bound to the 3'UTR of INPP4B; the mutated seed sites in miR-1290 abrogated this effect. Double knockdown of INPP4B and miR-1290 promoted CRC cell proliferation, suggesting miR-1290 promoted CRC cell proliferation by targeting INPP4B.
